label: tooth-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a tooth: small, short, broad-based and pointed. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991143 scale-like and FLOPO:0991200 bract-like, worded as they are; not PATO:0001205 dentated, which is bearing teeth.
reason: Sepals, auricles and staminodes reduced to tooth-like points are a frequent description with no term; 'toothlike' is also staged in eflora-foc and eflora-fop.

label: monomorphic
definition: A morphological quality inhering in a set of homologous plant structures by virtue of its members occurring in a single form. NOTE: Sibling and opposite of FLOPO:0991092 dimorphic.
reason: Homomorphic leaves or sporophylls are all of one form, the opposite of FLOPO dimorphic. This is the same class as 'monomorphic' proposed in curation/opus-review-2026-11-14/values.tsv and should be merged with it.
A hyphenated compound of two shapes is a continuum between lanceolate (PATO_0001877) and elliptic (PATO_0000947), as for linear-lanceolate and ovate-lanceolate.

label: trilete
definition: A shape quality inhering in a spore by virtue of its proximal face bearing a three-armed, Y-shaped laesura. NOTE: Sibling of monolete (a single straight laesura), which has no term either.
reason: A standard spore character of ferns and lycophytes, used only for spores, with no PATO or FLOPO term.
FLOPO subterranean already lists hypogeal as a related synonym. Hypogeal germination is read as the cotyledons staying below the ground, so the bearer is the cotyledon.
Indusiate = with an indusium. The FLOPO anatomy class exists; 'dépourvus d'indusie' is its absence, as with bracteate and ebracteate.

The value is the colour that follows ('stained purple'), and the word does not say whether it means a tinge, a blotch or a spot. As with 'marked' and 'covered', the colour word is annotated by itself.

target: new: colour of a marking (spotted PATO_0000333, with red PATO_0000322 as the colour of the spots)
reason: Two values of one bearer: the part is spotted and the spots are red. The colour belongs to the spots, not to the whole part, so it is neither a single term nor a continuum.
Bractless = without bracts, the same as ebracteate (rule C206).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (slot 1: part of the bearer = plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023) + red (PATO_0000322)
reason: The colour is red at the tip only. The apex goes in the part-of-bearer slot and red is the value, so no new term is needed.
'Involucral bracts' and 'bractées involucrales' name the PO class. Leaves 'becoming involucral' are leaves that form the involucre.
Epunctate = without dots, the negation of PATO punctate, in the same form as unlobed. The dots are mostly pellucid glands (FLOPO:0991174 gland-dotted), but the broader negation is safer.

target: docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md (new suffix 'glandular' -> gland, portion of secretory tissue PO_0005656; count 2)
reason: Bi-glandular = two glands, at the petiole apex or bract base where stated. The word has no term of its own, so it is split like 'bidentate'; 'glandular' still needs adding to config/flora_counted_parts.tsv.

label: polygamodioecious
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its belonging to a species whose individuals bear either staminate or pistillate flowers together with some bisexual flowers. NOTE: Follows FLOPO:0991072 dioecious and FLOPO:0991177 polygamous.
reason: A distinct and well-defined sexual system, mostly dioecious but with bisexual flowers. Neither dioecious nor polygamous alone says this.
A continuum between ovoid (PATO_0001891 ovate, synonym ovoid) and globose (PATO_0001499 spherical, synonym globular).
Not a continuum: an elongated cylinder is oblong in side view, so both hold at once. Cylindrical is the more specific 3-D shape, read the same way as caudate-acuminate.
Pulverulent = covered with powder, the same reading as 'powdery' (rule C343).

label: tumid
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being swollen and bulging outward, so that it is plump and full. NOTE: Not PATO:0001851 swollen, which is a transient abnormal enlargement, nor PATO:0002376 inflated, which is filled with air.
reason: Tumid seeds, valves and perianth blades are a common description. The two nearest PATO terms are pathological or air-filled; 'turgid' is staged in several floras with the same meaning.
Bean-shaped seeds, pyrenes and monolete spores are kidney-shaped, one side convex and the other flat or concave: PATO reniform (synonym kidney-shaped).

Pusticulate = covered in minute pustule-like bumps, mostly on spores and seeds. That matches FLOPO verruculose (very small wart-like projections) better than bullate, which is a blistered surface between veins.
A gamopetalous (sympetalous) corolla has its petals fused to one another, which is FLOPO connate, as for 'united' (rule C171). The petals of the corolla are the bearer.

label: trullate
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being trowel-shaped: angular at base, sides and apex, broadest below the middle, with the two lower sides shorter than the two upper sides. NOTE: Sibling of rhombic (broadest at the middle); PATO:0001938 rhomboid is defined as a 3-D spheroid.
reason: A standard leaf and bract outline in the Systematics Association scheme, used alongside rhombic and ovate. PATO's only angular-outline term is a 3-D spheroid.
Shredded bark comes off in strips, which FLOPO exfoliating covers. Shredded leaf bases, sheaths and ligules split into fibres, which is FLOPO:0991026 fibrous, and should get a separate rule.
French cochléiforme/cochléariforme sepals and thecae are spoon-shaped. Cochleate seeds are coiled like a snail shell, a different meaning, and stay outside this rule.
'Restricted to apices/nodes' is a position relative to another part, and the word carries no quality of its own. The location is the content and belongs to the relation pattern.
Most uses are 'lacunae present' in leaves, and PO plant anatomical space has lacuna as a synonym. A lacunose receptacle or endocarp is pitted, which is foveate (PATO_0002296, rule C179).
A continuum between orbicular (PATO_0001934, with the 'sub' value qualifier) and obovate (PATO_0001936).
A continuum between obovate (PATO_0001936) and orbicular (PATO_0001934).

label: starchy
definition: A composition quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its containing abundant starch as a stored food reserve.
reason: Starchy versus oily endosperm, and starchy roots and rhizomes, are standard characters with no PATO or FLOPO term.

Callate = bearing calli, but 'callus/calli' was rejected as a generic bearer word (config/flora_rejected_bearer_words.tsv). The orchid lip callus, the grass floret callus and achene calli are different parts, and 'pair of calli' is a count once the part is resolved.
